facts.text: ALAA states that the Australian Labradoodle currently lacks AKC recognition, and that ALAA keeps its own breed standard for temperament, structure, coat, and type. ALAA also states that OFA has a separate breed code so Australian Labradoodle health records can be stored apart from Labrador or Poodle records. ALAA says consumer DNA breed tests are a poor substitute for a documented multigenerational pedigree.

facts.source: Australian Labradoodle Association of America, generation FAQ
facts.text: ALAA: F1 is a first cross of a purebred Poodle to a purebred Labrador Retriever, with mixed results, often moderate to low shedding and a sparse-hair to fleece coat. F1B is that F1 backcrossed to a purebred Poodle. An Australian Labradoodle, in ALAA's definition, carries Labrador, Poodle, and Cocker Spaniel (American or English). A multigenerational Australian Labradoodle is an Australian Labradoodle bred to another Australian Labradoodle. ALAA's purebred label starts after four consecutive like-to-like Australian Labradoodle matings. ALAA notes that AKC's foundation service looks for four generations of like-to-like matings.

facts.source: Australian Labradoodle Association (Australia), coat types and breed standard
facts.text: Australian Labradoodle Association size classes: standard 21 to 24 inches and 21 to 30 kg, medium 17 to 20 inches and 13 to 20 kg, miniature 14 to 16 inches and 7 to 13 kg. Coat page https://australianlabradoodleassoc.org.au/labradoodle-coat-types/ describes fleece (soft, wavy or curly, angora-like), wool (dense, lamb-like, mildly to very curly), and hair (short wiry to long, sheds, odor, seen in early generations, called a major fault). Desired coat length 4 to 6 inches, straight, wavy, or in spirals. A single coat is the aim. A double coat is listed as a fault.
